region.text: Tunisia, pacified between April 1881 and May 1882

region.text: Tunisia, the protectorate of the Treaty of Bardo

ledger.note: 12 May 1881: Tunisia becomes a French protectorate. region.text: Porto-Novo (protectorate), 1882

region.text: Guinea, occupied by France in 1884

region.text: Senegal, Mali, Ivory Coast and Benin cells added in Cliopatria's 1885 shape (page silent)

region.text: French Somaliland, the Gadabuursi and Issa protectorates

ledger.note: March 1885: France takes protectorates over the Somali clans of the Gulf of Tadjoura. region.text: Antsiranana (Diego-Suarez) on the northern coast of Madagascar

region.text: Ivory Coast and Central African Republic cells added in Cliopatria's 1890 shape (page silent)

ledger.note: 1890: the Ivory Coast coast (+79 cells) and a first strip of the Central African Republic (+11 cells) are added. region.text: Cotonou, where the Dahomey army stormed the French stockade on 4 March 1890

region.text: Cotonou

region.text: Cotonou, ceded by Dahomey

ledger.note: 3 October 1890: Dahomey cedes Cotonou to France. 'Béhanzin was also forced to cede Cotonou, but did receive 20,000 francs a year for giving up his customs rights.' region.text: the kingdom of Dahomey from the coast to Abomey

ledger.note: 4 July 1892: the second Franco-Dahomean war begins. 'on 4 July, the first shots of the war were fired from French gunboats with the shelling of several villages along the lower Ouémé Valley'; the French army moved inland in mid-August and entered Abomey on 17 November 1892.

region.text: Sultanate of Bangassou (protectorate), 1894

region.text: Dahomey (Benin), defeated by the French in 1894

ledger.note: 15 January 1894: Dahomey falls and passes to France. 'King Béhanzin surrendered to the French on 15 January 1894'; the page gives no annexation date and lists 'French Dahomey' from 1894. region.text: Gabon, Congo and Central African Republic cells added in Cliopatria's 1895 shape (page silent)

region.text: the Algerian cells added in Cliopatria's 1895 shape (page silent)

region.text: Madagascar, the capital Antananarivo taken

region.text: the Malagasy Protectorate under Queen Ranavalona III

region.text: Madagascar, the Merina protectorate ended

region.text: Madagascar, an island colony after the monarchy ended in 1897

ledger.note: 1897: Madagascar is French land. The page gives 'in 1897' for the deposition of the queen and the end of the monarchy but does not say the word annexation; Cliopatria draws Madagascar from 1898. The island is 98% of Madagascar's cells in the 1898 shape.

region.text: Dar al Kuti around N'Delé in the north of the Central African Republic

region.text: Sultanate of Damagaram (protectorate), around Zinder

ledger.note: 1899: the Sultanate of Damagaram (Zinder) becomes a French protectorate (French Africa page: 'Sultanate of Damagaram (protectorate): 1899'). On 10 October 1899 French Sudan was divided among the coastal colonies (French Sudan page), an internal reorganisation.

region.text: the Chad and Niger cells added in Cliopatria's 1900 shape

ledger.note: 1900: Chad is organised. The French Africa page lists 'Chad 1900-1960'; Cliopatria's 1900 step adds Chad (+440 cells), Niger (+251) and Cameroon (+105). The page names no state that held the land.

region.text: the Hoggar Mountains, the kingdom of Kel Ahaggar

region.text: the Hoggar Mountains, the kingdom of Kel Ahaggar

region.text: the Wadai heartland around Abéché

region.text: Abéché, which the French occupied in June 1909

ledger.note: June 1909: the French take Abéché. region.text: the Wadai heartland around Abéché

ledger.note: October 1911: Dud Murra surrenders. The campaign 'succeeded in forcing Dud Murra to surrender in October 1911' and Adam Asil was ousted by the French in 1911; the occupation of Wadai was completed in 1912.

region.text: Neukamerun, the slice of Middle Congo (and neighbouring Gabon and Ubangi-Shari) ceded to German Kamerun

region.text: Dar al Kuti around N'Delé in the north of the Central African Republic

region.text: Dar al Kuti around N'Delé in the north of the Central African Republic

ledger.note: 1912: France annexes Dar al Kuti. region.text: Abéché, which the French occupied in June 1909

region.text: German Kamerun, invaded from French Equatorial Africa

region.text: German Togoland, invaded from Dahomey and the Gold Coast

region.text: German Togoland, surrendered 27 August 1914

ledger.note: 27 August 1914: Togoland surrenders. 'The colony surrendered without conditions with British and French troops landing in Kamina on 27 August 1914', after five days of fighting.

region.text: Togoland, occupied by British and French troops

ledger.note: 27 August 1914: Britain and France occupy Togoland. The surrender of 27 August leads to an Anglo-French occupation; the land is divided into French and British zones in 1916 (27 December 1916). Cliopatria draws the French zone as French land from 1915.

region.text: Neukamerun, occupied by Belgian and French troops in 1915

region.text: the French zone of Kamerun under the February 1916 partition

ledger.note: February 1916: France and Britain agree to divide Kamerun. 'In February 1916, before the campaign ended, Britain and France agreed to divide Kamerun' (the Picot Provisional Partition Line); By mid-February the last German garrison at Mora surrendered.

region.text: Kamerun, the campaign ended 10 March 1916

ledger.note: 10 March 1916: the Kamerun campaign ends in Allied victory. Infobox 'Date: 6 August 1914 - 10 March 1916'; the Germans retreated into Spanish Río Muni in early 1916 and Mora surrendered in mid-February.

region.text: Neukamerun, the slice of Gabon, Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari that France ceded to Germany in November 1911 and re-occupied in 1915

region.text: Neukamerun, the slice of Gabon, Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari that France ceded to Germany in November 1911 and re-occupied in 1915

ledger.note: 1919: Neukamerun is French land again, inside the AEF colonies. region.text: French Cameroon under the League of Nations mandate

region.text: French Cameroon under the League of Nations mandate

ledger.note: 1919: French Cameroon becomes French land under the League of Nations mandate. 'The former German colony became the League of Nations mandates of French Cameroon and British Cameroon'; the dossier draws the mandate as direct land, as Cliopatria does.

region.text: French Togoland under the League of Nations mandate

ledger.note: 20 July 1922: French Togoland becomes a League of Nations mandate. The page gives 'League of Nations mandate 20 July 1922'; 'a French colonial League of Nations mandate from 1922 to 1946'. The mandate is not annexation; Cliopatria draws Togo as direct land.

region.text: French Togoland under the League of Nations mandate

ledger.note: 20 July 1922: French Togoland becomes French land under the League of Nations mandate. The page gives 'League of Nations mandate 20 July 1922' and 'a French colonial League of Nations mandate from 1922 to 1946'; the dossier draws the mandate as direct land, as Cliopatria does.

region.text: French Cameroon

ledger.note: August 1940: French Cameroon rallies to the Free French. 'French Cameroon and most of the AEF rallied to the Free French Forces in August 1940.'

region.text: Chad, Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari, the AEF colonies that rallied

ledger.note: August 1940: Chad, Middle Congo and Ubangi-Shari rally to the Free French. The page says 'most of the AEF rallied' in August 1940 and only Gabon stayed with Vichy, so these three are the rest; the page does not name them.

region.text: Gabon, held for Vichy until 12 November 1940

ledger.note: November 1940: the Free French attack Vichy Gabon. The French West Africa page: 'Gabon fell to Free France after the Battle of Gabon in November 1940'; the French Equatorial Africa page: 'Gabon instead remained loyal to Vichy France until 12 November 1940'. The page gives no start day.

region.text: Gabon, Vichy until 12 November 1940

ledger.note: 12 November 1940: Gabon falls to the Free French. 'Gabon instead remained loyal to Vichy France until 12 November 1940.'

region.text: Gabon

ledger.note: 12 November 1940: Gabon passes to the Free French. 'Gabon instead remained loyal to Vichy France until 12 November 1940'; 'Gabon fell to Free France after the Battle of Gabon in November 1940' (French West Africa page).

region.text: the eastern Tunisian cells the Axis held until May 1943 (Cliopatria's 1943 shape lacks them)

ledger.note: November 1942: Axis forces occupy the east of Tunisia. 'French opposition to the Torch landings had ceased, creating a military vacuum in Tunisia' (10 November 1942); 40 German aircraft were at Tunis by 9 November, an airlift began on 12 November and the page dates the campaign from 17 November 1942. region.text: French Somaliland (Djibouti), occupied by Britain

ledger.note: 28 December 1942: Britain occupies French Somaliland. Infobox 'British occupation: December 28, 1942'; 'Italian invasion: June 18, 1940'. region.text: French Somaliland, back under French rule

ledger.note: 1943: French rule returns to Djibouti. region.text: the Free French lands reappearing in Cliopatria's 1943 shape, without Djibouti (page silent)

ledger.note: 1943: the Free French lands rejoin the shape. region.text: the eastern Tunisian cells missing from Cliopatria's 1943 shape, the Axis-held part until May 1943

27 October 1946: the French Empire becomes the French Union. 'The French Empire was renamed the French Union on 27 October 1946'; the French Somaliland page adds that its status changed to overseas territory on 27 October 1946. Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: the Fezzan-Ghadames military territory, joining the Kingdom of Libya

ledger.note: 24 December 1951: the Fezzan passes to the Kingdom of Libya. The Fezzan-Ghadames territory was 'occupied and administered by Free France from 1943 until Libya gained independence in 1951', 'to form the Kingdom of Libya on 24 December 1951'. Cliopatria drops the cells only in 1953.

region.text: the French zone of Morocco

ledger.note: 2 March 1956: France recognises Moroccan independence. The protectorate ended 'with the dissolution of the Treaty of Fez on 2 March 1956' through the Franco-Moroccan Joint Declaration; the Spanish zone followed on 7 April 1956 and Tangier on 29 October 1956.

region.text: the protectorate of Tunisia

ledger.note: 20 March 1956: Tunisia becomes independent. 'The protectorate was finally abolished on 20 March 1956.'

region.text: all French colonial Africa remaining in 1957: Algeria, French West Africa, French Equatorial Africa, Madagascar, Cameroon, Togo, Somaliland, the Comoros

ledger.note: 1957: Cliopatria's French Africa row ends and its land continues in the French Fifth Republic row from 1958. The pages show the federations lasting longer: 'The federation existed from 1895 until 1958' and 'Legally, the federation ceased to exist after the 1958 French constitutional referendum' (French West Africa), 'September 1958 referendum' for the AEF; independence followed in 1960 (Togo on 27 April, the Mali Federation on 20 June, the AEF republics in August) and in Algeria in 1962. The end year 1957 is the row's, confidence 1.

wars.name: French conquest of Tunisia

zones.text: Tunisia, invaded from the north on 24 April 1881 and occupied in full by May 1882

wars.outcome: French victory: the Treaty of Bardo of 12 May 1881 makes Tunisia a protectorate; the Sfax revolt (June-July 1881) and Kairouan (August-October) are put down and 'May 1882: Occupation of the whole country was completed'.

wars.name: Franco-Hova Wars
wars.outcome: First war 1883-1885: the Treaty of Tamatave (17 December 1885) cedes Diego-Suarez and gives France Malagasy foreign policy. Second war from 12 December 1894: Antananarivo falls on 1 October 1895 and Madagascar becomes a protectorate; the monarchy is dissolved in 1897.
wars.note: Infobox 'December 1883 - September 1895'; 'The British recognized a French Protectorate of Madagascar in September 1890'.

wars.name: French conquest of the Sudan

zones.text: the upper Senegal and Niger valleys (the Upper River colony of 1880, French Sudan from 1890)

wars.outcome: 'French conquest began in 1879'; the Upper River colony 'Established c. 1880'; Kayes fort 1881; renamed French Sudan on 18 August 1890; 'In 1893, French Sudan formally came under civilian administration'.
wars.note: The page names no opposing state; the dossier lists the opponents as chiefdoms. Segou 1890 and Timbuktu 1894 are not on the page.

wars.name: First Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: by the treaty of 3 October 1890 Dahomey cedes Cotonou and recognises Porto-Novo as a French protectorate.
wars.note: 21 February to 4 October 1890 (infobox); the Cotonou stockade was stormed on 4 March. Hostilities resumed in July 1892.

wars.name: Second Franco-Dahomean War

zones.text: the kingdom of Dahomey from the coast to Abomey

wars.outcome: French victory: French troops entered Abomey on 17 November 1892 and Béhanzin surrendered on 15 January 1894; Dahomey became French (the page lists 'French Dahomey' from 1894).
wars.note: Renamed from 'French conquest of Dahomey' to the page's title. First shots 4 July 1892, inland advance from mid-August, battle at Dogba on 19 September. The Scramble for Africa page gives only 'Behanzin's mediatic defeat against the French in 1894'; the French West Africa page says Dahomey was 'put under colonial tutelage in 1892' and joined the federation in 1904.

wars.name: Mokrani Revolt
wars.outcome: 'The most serious native insurrection since the time of Abd al-Qadir was the 1871 Mokrani Revolt in the Kabylia'; 'By April 1871, 250 tribes had risen'; the surviving commanders were tried in Constantine in 1873. No border moved.

wars.name: French conquest of the Algerian Sahara

zones.text: the Hoggar Mountains, kingdom of Kel Ahaggar

wars.outcome: 'In 1902, a French military expedition entered Hoggar Mountains and defeated Kel Ahaggar in a battle in Tit'; 'The conquest of the Saharan lands in Algeria finished in 1903'.

wars.name: Wadai War

zones.text: the Wadai heartland around Abéché; the whole sultanate was annexed in 1912

wars.outcome: French victory: Abéché occupied in June 1909, Dud Murra surrendered in October 1911 and 'Wadai was completely occupied by the French in 1912'.
wars.note: Open conflict from 1906 (no month); French defeats at Wadi Kadja (4 January 1910) and Dorothe (8 November 1910); some native rulers kept de facto independence to 1917 and open resistance lasted to 1920.

wars.name: Agadir Crisis

zones.text: Neukamerun, the slice of Middle Congo ceded to Germany

wars.outcome: Diplomatic: 'the deployment of the German gunboat Panther to the port of Agadir in July 1911'; in November 1911 Germany accepted France's position in Morocco 'in return for a slice of territory in the French Equatorial African colony of Middle Congo'.

wars.name: Togoland campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: French troops landed at Little Popo on 6 August 1914, the colony was invaded on 26 August and surrendered 'without conditions' on 27 August 1914; divided into French and British zones on 27 December 1916.

wars.name: Kamerun campaign

zones.text: Neukamerun, occupied by Belgian and French troops in 1915

wars.outcome: Allied victory ('6 August 1914 - 10 March 1916'): Douala surrendered on 27 September 1914, the Germans withdrew to Spanish Río Muni in early 1916; Britain and France agreed to divide Kamerun in February 1916 and the League of Nations mandates followed in 1919.

wars.name: Rif War
wars.outcome: 'A coalition of France and Spain finally defeated the rebels in 1925'; Lyautey's tenure ran 'in the middle of the failed revolt of the Republic of the Rif'. No French border moved.

wars.name: Battles of Dakar
wars.outcome: French West Africa 'declared allegiance to the Vichy regime' against the Free French Forces 'in July and September 1940' (the two battles of Dakar). No border moved.

wars.name: Battle of Gabon
wars.outcome: Free French victory: 'Gabon fell to Free France after the Battle of Gabon in November 1940'; 'Gabon instead remained loyal to Vichy France until 12 November 1940'.

wars.name: Tunisia campaign

zones.text: the eastern Tunisian cells missing from Cliopatria's 1943 shape (Axis-held part)

wars.outcome: Axis forces held the east of Tunisia from November 1942 (campaign 17 November 1942 to 13 May 1943); Tunis and Bizerte fell on 7 May and the last Axis surrender was on 13 May 1943, when the Bey was also deposed by Free French authorities.
wars.note: Renamed to the page's title. The zone is the 76 eastern cells that Cliopatria's 1943 shape lacks; the occupation events of November 1942 and May 1943 carry the same zone.

wars.name: Free French occupation of the Fezzan
wars.outcome: Free French forces from Chad 'moved north from Chad to take control of the territory in January 1943' with British approval; administered until 24 December 1951.
wars.note: The page names no opposing force and does not mention Leclerc, Kufra, Murzuk or Sebha.

wars.name: Algerian War
wars.outcome: Clipped to this dossier's end (1957) by the reviewer; the war continues in the french-fifth-republic dossier. 'The Algerian War ran from 1954 to 1962'; Evian Accords of 18 March 1962; independence on 5 July 1962, after this dossier's end in 1957 (Algeria stays inside the French Fifth Republic row until then).

certainty.note: Coastal posts, river basins and the Algerian south have no surveyed limits on the pages opened; the Tunisian protectorate of 1881 is the one fixed state, its frontiers not on the pages.

Interior claims by occupation. The Franco-Portuguese Convention of 1886 settled the borders of Guinea-Bissau and the 1890 Anglo-French agreement a diplomatic solution (Scramble for Africa page): those lines are sharp. The conquest page: 'it was not until 1903 that France fully secured its colonial borders'.

Colony boundaries follow decrees (Mauritania and Niger 1904, Upper Volta 1921), treaties (Fes 1912, the November 1911 cession of Neukamerun) and agreed partition lines (Kamerun February 1916, Togoland 27 December 1916). The pages opened give no survey for the Saharan frontiers with Libya and Spanish Sahara, which stay soft.

notes:
french-africa (af-08-b). Cliopatria's French Africa row (1846-1957, 38 shapes) is a composite of every French colony in Africa: Algeria from 1848 (French Algeria 1830-1847 is a separate row), the Senegal posts, Tunisia, Morocco, Madagascar, the AOF and AEF and the Cameroon and Togo mandates. The 14 pages budgeted were opened; none failed to load. Kamerun is a separate dossier.

Decisions. (1) Type colony, family france, no capital: the entity has no single seat; the pages give only the federation capitals Saint-Louis 1895-1902 and Dakar 1902-1960 (AOF), Brazzaville (AEF), Algiers (Algeria). (2) The end year 1957 is Cliopatria's: the row continues as French Fifth Republic from 1958 (11.26 M km2 in 1958-1959, 8.47 M in 1960, 3.03 M in 1961-2023 with Algeria still inside, which the eu-22 dossier should correct); the federations legally ended in 1958 and the territories became independent in 1960 (Algeria 1962). The dissolve event is confidence 1. (3) Protectorates (Tunisia 1881, Morocco 1912) are recorded as gains, as the sibling dossiers beylik-of-tunis and morocco record them as dissolve/loss to french-africa; Madagascar 1895-1897, a protectorate for two years before annexation, and Dar al Kuti 1897-1912 are vassal tints. League of Nations mandates (Togo 1922, Cameroon 1919) end an occupation event and are drawn as direct land, as in Cliopatria. (4) Where Cliopatria lags the pages, new keyframes carry the correction (Tunisia 1881-1884, Dahomey 1894, Madagascar 1897, the end of the Fezzan 1951) and the Free French years 1940-1943 are corrected by removing Chad; very small enclaves (Diego-Suarez 1885, Cotonou 1868, Porto-Novo 1882, Djibouti 1885, Togoland 1914) are carried by the ledger alone.

Unexplained or unverified Cliopatria steps, kept at confidence 1: 1849 Gabon, 1853 Senegal, 1856 Mali, 1859 and 1860 Senegal basin and Mauritania, 1870 (the Algerian cells rise from 9% to 20%), 1885 and 1890 small steps, 1895 (Gabon, Congo, Ubangi and Algeria), 1905 Libya block (534 cells), 1911 Chad (+1,032 cells), 1920 Libya block lost (490 cells), 1943 reunion of the Free French lands, and the cell noise of 1922-1939. No opened page covers the Territoires du Sud of Algeria, the conquest of Chad, the end of Wadai, the Libyan frontier in the Sahara, the changes of Upper Volta before 1921, Madagascar in 1942, or Operation Torch.

Disagreements between pages. The French Africa list gives French Upper Volta 1896 while the AOF page says Upper Volta was divided from French Sudan in 1921; Oubangui-Chari 1905 against Cliopatria's Central African Republic from 1895; Mauritania joins the AOF in 1920 (AOF page) but is a Military Territory in 1904; the Kayes fort is 1881 and the colony 1880; the Morocco infobox ends the protectorate on 7 April 1956 and its text on 2 March 1956; Algiers is the capital of Algeria in the infobox. The French Africa page's Comoros 1866 does not match Mayotte 1841.

Overlaps for the orchestrator. Free French 1940-1943 (Cliopatria) draws only 57% of Chad in 1941-1943; this dossier removes all of Chad from French Africa for 1940-1942, so free-french should take the whole country. Counterparts without a dossier: Kel Ahaggar, Dar al Kuti, Sultanate of Bangassou, Sultanate of Damagaram, Emirate of Trarza, Emirate of Adrar, Taganit confederation, the Gadabuursi and Issa clans, Porto-Novo, Cotonou, Upper Senegal chiefdoms, Guinea chiefdoms. Regions the gazetteer lacks: Neukamerun (expressed here as the difference of two Cliopatria shapes), British Togoland, Hoggar (Ahaggar), Territoires du Sud; the Hoggar is carried by the admin1 'Tamanghasset'.

Areas. Infobox figures: AOF 4,689,000 km2 and AEF 2,500,000 km2 (undated), Algeria 585,814 km2 (1899) and 2,381,741 km2 (1962), Tunisia 155,000 km2, French Sudan 1,241,238 km2 (1959). The shapes agree within the factor of two everywhere they could be compared: 1905 ratio 0.98, 1870 Algerian part 0.78, 1895 Algerian part 1.6.
